lyrics:
[Intro: clipped off-beat electric guitar, bubbly synth bass, claps]

[Verse 1: conversational, twangy, light beat]
Pulled up to the place in a borrowed dress
Forty-one, first night out since the whole big mess
Everybody's shiny, everybody knows the host
I'm holding up the wall like a second coat

[Pre-Chorus: drums build, voice tightens]
My stomach's doing cartwheels, I'm checking the door
Thinking "what did I even come here for?"
Then the DJ fades one out, and oh

[Chorus: big, bright, gang vocals on the title]
And then my song came on
And my shoulders came down
And my hips said yes
And I forgot this town
Put my drink in the air
Like I'm seventeen
Yeah, and then my song came on
And it was all okay
It was all okay

[Verse 2: conversational, more confident]
Now my dad wants Motown and my niece wants the new
The DJ's got a headache and I've lost a shoe
Some guy in a waistcoat wants to teach me how to spin
I say "honey, I invented it," and pull my sister in

[Pre-Chorus: drums build, voice tightens]
Was a minute I was sinking, I was halfway out
Had the car keys in my fingers and a head full of doubt
Then the speakers gave a crackle, and oh

[Chorus: big, bright, gang vocals on the title]
And then my song came on
And my shoulders came down
And my hips said yes
And I forgot this town
Put my drink in the air
Like I'm seventeen
Yeah, and then my song came on
And it was all okay
It was all okay

[Bridge: half-time, soft, electric piano]
Three minutes and a half
That's all it ever takes
To put me back together
In all the broken places

[Final Chorus: full band, key hits, crowd singing]
And then my song came on
And my shoulders came down
And my hips said yes
And I forgot this town
Put my drink in the air
Like I'm seventeen
Yeah, and then my song came on
And it was all okay
It was all okay

[Outro: guitar and claps, shouted over the music]
Play it again
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 96 BPM, 4/4, F-sharp major. A mid-tempo bounce with a reggae-style off-beat guitar. Sunny, easy and a bit nervous at first.

VOICE: Female, bright and slightly raspy with a southern country twang, conversational in the verses as if telling a friend the story. Stronger and more open in the chorus, where a group of friends shouts the title line with her.

INSTRUMENTS: A clean electric guitar playing clipped chords on the off-beats. A bubbly, bouncing synth bass. A simple pop drum kit with a fat snare and handclaps. Glossy synth pads. An electric piano in the bridge. A second guitar with light crunch in the final chorus.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, guitar, bass and claps. 0:10 Verse 1. 0:30 Pre-chorus. 0:45 Chorus 1. 1:10 Verse 2. 1:30 Pre-chorus. 1:45 Chorus 2. 2:10 Bridge, half time and soft. 2:30 Final chorus with the crowd. 2:55 Tag, the last two lines repeated. 3:08 Outro, guitar and claps, a shouted request at 3:20.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Late-2000s pop: clean, bright and friendly, guitar and bass tightly locked, vocal up front with the twang left in.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The half-second of near silence after 'and oh', before the chorus lands.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: She is forty-one and it is her first night out after something hard. The song that saves her is an old one. Listeners who were teenagers in 2009 will recognise both the feeling and the age.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Dread, rescue, swagger, gratitude.
